children: Arunish Chawla says the share purchase agreement protects existing employees against adverse changes as staff unions prepare to protest the divestment

Service conditions of existing employees at IDBI Bank will remain unchanged following the proposed sale of the lender to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings, according to Arunish Chawla, Secretary of the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM).Chawla said employees and pensioners had “nothing to fear” from the sale, which involves the divestment of more than 60 per cent of the bank’s holding for Rs 52,878 crore.

“As per the share purchase agreement, the service conditions of the existing employees cannot be changed, modified or altered to their disadvantage by the strategic buyer,” Chawla told PTI.His remarks come amid protests by IDBI Bank employees against the government’s divestment move. Bank staff have called for a strike across branches in early November, with the United Forum of Bank Unions also extending support to the proposed action.
Addressing concerns among pensioners, Chawla said a dedicated pension fund had been set aside and that all commitments would continue to be honoured.

He also clarified that IDBI Bank is not a nationalised bank and that the service conditions of its employees are determined by the bank’s board in consultation with employees, rather than directly by the Union government.
Chawla said the lender would continue to operate as a board-managed company after the transaction, with its operations governed by applicable company and labour laws.

“IDBI Bank is being restructured as a going concern and even in future it will be a board-managed company. It works under the company and labour law today; it will continue to work under the company and labour law tomorrow,” he said.
